# Electron
Electron is a framework for building desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. By embedding [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) and [[NodeJS]] into its binary, Electron allows you to maintain one JavaScript codebase and create cross-platform apps that work on Windows, macOS, and Linux 

![electron](data:image/png;base64,)
## Electron.NET
Electron.NET is a **wrapper** around a native Electron application with an embedded ASP.NET Core application. Via Electron.NET IPC bridge it can invoke Electron APIs from .NET.
### Initialization
To add Electron support to .NET minimal API project we should install `ElectronNET.CLI` dotnet tool:
``` cmd
dotnet tool install ElectronNET.CLI -g
```
Then navigate to the project and run the the following:
``` cmd
electronize init
```
This command will generate electron manifest file and will setup the project to copy this manifest to output directory:
``` xml
<ItemGroup>
	<Content Update="electron.manifest.json">
		<CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>
	</Content>
</ItemGroup>
```
Then we need to install `ElectronNET.API` NuGet package and modify application entry point like this:
``` csharp
using ElectronNET.API;
using ElectronNET.API.Entities;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.WebHost.UseElectron();
builder.Services.AddElectron();

var app = builder.Build();

await app.StartAsync();
await Electron.WindowManager.CreateWindowAsync();

app.WaitForShutdown();
```
After that the app can be run in the electron window with the next command:
``` cmd
electronize start /watch
```
